def is_plain_name(name: str) -> bool:
    """True when name is a single plain file name: non-empty, not "." or "..", and with no path separators or NUL characters."""
    ex is_plain_name("a.txt") == True
    ex is_plain_name("") == False
    ex is_plain_name("..") == False
    ex is_plain_name("../secret") == False
    ex is_plain_name("/etc/passwd") == False
    ex is_plain_name("sub\\x") == False
    if name == "" or name == "." or name == "..":
        return False
    if "/" in name or "\\" in name or "\0" in name:
        return False
    return True

def plain_names(names: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """The names that are plain file names, in their original order."""
    post out.len() <= names.len()
    ex plain_names([]) == []
    ex plain_names(["../secret", "a.txt", "/etc/passwd", "b.txt"]) == ["a.txt", "b.txt"]
    out: list[str] = []
    for n in names:
        if is_plain_name(n):
            out.append(n.copy())
    return out

def first_readable(names: list[str]) -> str uses fs:
    """Text of the first name in names that can be read from the directory notes, or "" when none can. Runs with fs confined to notes via fs.sub; names that are not plain file names, and missing or unreadable files, are skipped, so nothing outside notes is ever read."""
    safe = plain_names(names)
    with fs = fs.sub("notes"):
        for n in safe:
            text: str | None = fs.read_text(n) else None
            if text is not None:
                return text
    return ""
